comments.body:
Report landed at docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md (commit 143d5074e). Key results:
- Research verified: CMU-CS-25-132 +24% decomposition gain (12-subtask empirical cap); IBM 2605.15425 static decomposition WORSE than monolithic, runtime-structured -51.7%/-73.3% retry tokens; CodePlan 5/7 vs 0/7; FixedBench 35-65% over-action; CooperBench -30% coordination penalty vs CAID/Shepherd structured gains; Tricorder <10% FP trust cliff; CORE -25.8% FP via verify pass; AQUSA 93.8R/72.2P deterministic ceiling; ambiguity does NOT predict failure but incompleteness/inconsistency do.
- OSS convergence (15 systems, file-level): plan/execute pause, dependency DAG as checkable field, atomicity=reviewability (not size), verification as required structured field, self-contained task packets; contested: parallel-vs-sequential default, rigid grammar vs prose, numeric sizing (almost nobody has one).
- Store history: 1,897 plan reviews/527 tickets, PASS 47%/BLOCK 45%, 30% of candidate findings dropped by pass 2/3, 68% of tickets >=2 rounds, 92% of BLOCKed tickets converge to PASS. Post-claim description edits: 16/505 (3.2%), 15 substantive; of 8 with persisted reviews: 3 MISSED (all asserted-capability-of-existing-module grounding, incl. 1 via bug exemption), 4 CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED (advisory latency), 1 UNKNOWABLE.
- 7 recommendations (R1-R7) in report section 6, each pass-scoped with falsifiable experiment + FP assessment: asserted-capability probe (P1), operator-attested lint (P1/DET), decomposition-shape container criterion (P1), necessity/no-op gate + bug-tier pilot (P1), agentic capability sub-answer (P2), advisory-triage move (P4), gate-eval instrumentation (cross-cutting; extends docs/experiments/plan-review-gate).

compiled_state.description:
## Why
The plan-review gate (pass 1 finding discovery, pass 2 validation/impact, pass 4 coaching) measures plan quality against packaged criteria. We want to assess it against the state of the art on AI task decomposition and produce recommendations that improve its ability to detect decomposition flaws in plans without raising false positives.

## What
1. Deep research on AI task decomposition: recent data-driven research (papers with data + code) and OSS community convergence observed in skills/prompts that decompose software-engineering tasks.
2. Synthesize with the two operator-supplied reports (~/Downloads/ai-task-decomposition-report.md and "AI Task Decomposition Best Practices.md") into a cited state-of-the-art report at docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md, with quoted prompts/code and specific data; commit it.
3. Map the report's practices onto what plan review measures today (criteria registry, DET floor, LLM criteria), respecting the strict pass 1 / pass 2 / pass 4 separation of concerns.
4. Produce recommendations, each with (a) a falsifiable experiment to validate improved flaw detection without added false positives, and (b) an assessment against this repo's actual plan-review history (attestations/review sidecars) for whether it would have generated valid findings or false positives.
5. Quantify the "ticket edited after entering in_progress" signal from store history as a proxy for plan-review misses, and use it to ground the recommendations.

## Prerequisites
- The two operator-supplied input reports have been verified present and read at execution time:
  - `~/Downloads/ai-task-decomposition-report.md` (sha256 e85aaac27ad511782772acb54f71e344806d38c08179f8e923eca458f8bd7d93)
  - `~/Downloads/AI Task Decomposition Best Practices.md` (sha256 32cc59125cb02dead4225f122c49792117a30c2ba2549a0d35c73afc19fd4a66)
- Both SHA-256 hashes are recorded in the SOTA report's sources section so the synthesis inputs are pinned and reproducible without committing the operator-supplied files themselves.
- Fallback: if either file is absent or its hash differs at any later re-execution, note the gap explicitly in the SOTA report's sources section and synthesize from the deep-research findings alone — do not fabricate content from a missing/changed file.

## Method for AC #5 (post-claim edit signal)
- Data: replay each work ticket's event stream in `.tickets-tracker/<id>/` (CREATE + EDIT + STATUS events, nanosecond-timestamped filenames).
- Signal: an EDIT event carrying a `fields.description` change with timestamp strictly after the ticket's first STATUS transition into `in_progress` and before any transition to `closed`.
- Materiality filter: only description/AC/file-impact changes count (matching the attestation material-fingerprint definition); tag/assignee/comment changes and `author == "reconciler"` (Jira echo) edits are excluded or reported separately.
- Confound acknowledged: `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim` was off for most of store history, so many tickets were never plan-reviewed at claim time; the analysis segments tickets by whether a prior REVIEW_RESULT exists and only draws missed-finding conclusions from the reviewed segment. Compaction (SNAPSHOT events) may hide early history for some tickets; those are excluded from the denominator.

## Scope / Files
- New file: docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md (the committed deliverable; recommendations included as a section).
- Read-only analysis of: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/ (the passes/orchestrator/DET floor), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (packaged registry), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ (packaged pass + criterion prompts), docs/plan-review-gate.md, and the tickets store history (REVIEW_RESULT sidecars + event streams; full history recovered from git objects of the tickets branch since the on-disk worktree is compacted).
- Non-goals: NO code changes to the gate in this task — recommendations only; implementation is follow-up work to be filed as discovered_from tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A report exists at docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md with citations, quoted code/prompts from OSS projects, and specific quantitative data, synthesizing independent research with the two Downloads reports.
- [ ] The report is committed on main with a rebar-ticket trailer referencing this ticket.
- [ ] The report contains a gap analysis mapping decomposition best practices to what plan-review passes 1, 2, and 4 each measure, keeping each recommendation scoped to the correct pass.
- [ ] At least 5 recommendations, each with a falsifiable experiment (metric + pass/fail condition) and a false-positive assessment grounded in actual plan-review history from this repo's store.
- [ ] The post-claim ticket-edit signal is quantified from store history and cited in at least one recommendation.

## Verification
Let `F=docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md`.
- AC1 (report exists, cites sources + pinned inputs, quotes prompts, carries data): `test -f $F && grep -q 'e85aaac27ad51178' $F && test $(grep -c 'arxiv.org' $F) -ge 8 && grep -q 'tasks-template.md' $F`
- AC2 (committed with trailer): `git log -1 --format=%B -- $F | grep -qi 'rebar-ticket: d39b'`
- AC3 (gap analysis scoped per pass): `grep -q 'Pass 1' $F && grep -q 'Pass 2' $F && grep -q 'Pass 4' $F && grep -qi 'gap analysis' $F`
- AC4 (≥5 recommendations, each with a falsifiable experiment + FP assessment): `test $(grep -c '^### R' $F) -ge 5 && test $(grep -ci 'falsifiable experiment' $F) -ge 5 && test $(grep -ci 'FP assessment' $F) -ge 5`
- AC5 (post-claim edit signal quantified + cited in a recommendation): `grep -q 'post-claim' $F && grep -Eq '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%' $F`
